q1.question: Do I need a big audience to start?
q1.answer: No. Pages work at every size — a handful of regular viewers who care about your golf is enough to begin.

q2.question: What can supporters fund?
q2.answer: Anything your content needs: green fees for a course review, editing time, travel to a shoot, or a specific item on your wish list.

q3.question: Does BuyMeATee replace my other platforms?
q3.answer: No — it sits alongside YouTube, Instagram or wherever you publish, giving your audience one clear place to get behind your goals.

q1.question: Can amateur golfers accept support?
q1.answer: Amateur status rules vary by governing body and change over time. Check the rules that apply to your competitions before accepting support — our blog guide to golf sponsorship for amateur players is a good place to start.

q2.question: What kinds of goals work best?
q2.answer: Specific, honest ones: a run of county events, a championship entry, a winter of coaching. Clear goals are easier to get behind than open-ended asks.

q3.question: Do supporters get anything back?
q3.answer: Support is a gift towards your goal, not an investment — what supporters get is the journey: your updates, your progress and a real part in the story.

cta.heading: Your season deserves supporters.

q1.question: Am I allowed to accept support as a college golfer?
q1.answer: Rules on outside support differ between countries, colleges and governing bodies, and they change. Check the regulations that apply to you before accepting support.

q2.question: What goals make sense for college golf?
q2.answer: Travel to qualifiers, training camps, a summer of amateur events back home — anything specific your season genuinely needs.

q1.question: What travel goals work best?
q1.answer: Specific legs of the journey: one championship abroad, a three-event swing, the ferry-and-fuel budget for a national season. Supporters love knowing which stop they made possible.

q2.question: Can I run more than one goal at a time?
q2.answer: Yes — you can have up to three goals live at once, so a travel goal can sit alongside a season or equipment goal.

q3.question: Which countries and currencies does BuyMeATee support?
q3.answer: Creators can set up payouts from a growing list of countries across ten currencies — you choose your country when you set up payments.

q1.question: What makes a good charity golf challenge?
q1.answer: Something concrete and a little bit mad: four rounds in a day, a hundred holes in a weekend, walking between courses. A vivid challenge with a clear goal is easy to get behind.

q2.question: How does the money reach the charity?
q2.answer: Support is paid to you as the page owner, and you pass it on to your chosen charity. Be clear on your page about where the money is going — supporters back your challenge because they trust you.

q3.question: Can a club or society run a charity challenge page?
q3.answer: Yes — captains' charities, society fundraisers and club challenge days all fit. One organiser runs the page and shares the story.

q1.question: How is this different from lesson fees?
q1.answer: It isn't a booking system. Support backs the goals that sit around your work — competing in pro-ams, new teaching technology, free junior clinics — not the lessons themselves.

q2.question: What goals resonate with members?
q2.answer: Ones the club benefits from or can be proud of: representing the club in regional events, a covered teaching bay, a junior development programme.

q3.question: Can assistants and PGA trainees use BuyMeATee?
q3.answer: Yes — exam costs, playing-ability tests and tournament starts are exactly the kind of goals a supportive membership loves to get behind.

q1.question: Do I need to make videos to use BuyMeATee?
q1.answer: No. Any coaching goal works — a covered bay, a junior programme, a training aid library. Content is one path, not the price of entry.

q2.question: What do supporters get for backing a coach?
q2.answer: A front-row seat: your updates, your progress and the knowledge that the clinics and content they enjoy exist because they backed them.

q3.question: Does this compete with my lesson income?
q3.answer: No — it funds the things lessons don't: the equipment, projects and free sessions that grow your reputation and your community.

q1.question: Our podcast is small. Is it worth it?
q1.answer: Yes. Podcast audiences are loyal out of all proportion to their size — a few dozen regular listeners can carry a season's hosting and kit.

q2.question: What should a podcast goal fund?
q2.answer: Whatever the show genuinely needs: microphones and acoustic treatment, editing, hosting fees, or travel to record at the events you cover.

q3.question: How do we thank supporters?
q3.answer: However fits your show — updates on your page, a word of thanks on air, or simply making the better episodes their backing paid for.
